v.why: If edge 1->3 is none and edge 1->2 is none, node 1 has no outgoing path, so adding a conv on edge 0 is wasted; with e4 present the conv feeds the output directly.
Removing the input-to-output skip connection destroys the residual path that deep stacked cells rely on, hurting more than removing a conv on that edge.
Adding a residual shortcut helps most in conv-heavy cells that are otherwise hard to optimize, and helps little in parameter-free all-skip or all-pool cells.
Adding a conv where there was no edge both adds capacity and connects node 2 to the output, whereas replacing an existing skip or pool adds less.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the last edge with a skip removes the main learned transformation into the output, which hurts more than replacing other ops.
Without the 0->3 skip, the remaining paths to the output carry more of the signal, so deleting edge 1->3 hurts more.
In an otherwise empty cell, edge 3 is the only path, so a conv there adds essential capacity; in conv-rich cells, swapping the skip for a conv removes the useful residual.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on edge 0 removes more capacity than deleting a parameter-free skip on edge 0.
If edge 2->3 is none, node 2 is a dead end, so adding a conv on edge 1->2 cannot affect the output.
When edge 1->2 is absent, edge 0->2 is node 2's only input, so removing it kills the path through edge 5 and causes a larger drop.
